caseStudies.scale: 2024 operating earnings $47.4bn; paid $26.8bn US income tax; one cash dividend since 1965 (1967)
caseStudies.lesson: Subsidiaries keep their managers, but cash goes to the parent and the parent alone decides where it goes next. Copy: one owner allocation screen, managers run day to day, bonuses tied to profit above a target.

caseStudies.scale: FY2024 revenue $23.9bn, net earnings $3.9bn, free cash flow $5.3bn
caseStudies.lesson: A shared operating system (the Danaher Business System) is run in every unit, and free cash funds the next purchase. Copy: one group-wide upgrade tree that lifts every business, and buy/build only from free cash.

caseStudies.scale: Group revenue $5.4bn in 2022, target about $30bn by 2025; cement about 75% of revenue (2024 report)
caseStudies.lesson: One cash-cow business funds backward integration (sugar, refinery) to cut import and FX costs. Copy: each new business exists because an older one overpays for an input, and the cash cow pays for it.

caseStudies.scale: FY2024 revenue N407.9bn (power 82.8%, hotels 17.2%), profit after tax N94bn, dividend N1.00/share
caseStudies.lesson: A listed parent with a separately listed hotel arm: outside shareholders own part of each subsidiary, so dividends are shared. Copy: list a subsidiary, keep control above 51%, share its dividend pro rata.

groupRules.name: Month-end waterfall
groupRules.rule: Each business pays in order: salaries, loan repayments, tax (30% income tax + 4% levy on profit, 0% if turnover <=N50m), then keeps 30% of after-tax profit as reserve; the rest (70%) goes up to the parent.
groupRules.simplifiedFrom: Nigeria Tax Act 2025 rates (30% CIT, 4% development levy, small company 0%) and normal dividend practice

groupRules.name: Internal loan
groupRules.rule: Parent or any business may lend to another at 1% per game month (12%/yr), term 1 to 12 months, max 50% of the lender's cash. Unpaid at term: 10% of borrower's daily income auto-repays until cleared.
groupRules.simplifiedFrom: Arm's-length intercompany loans under Nigeria's Transfer Pricing Regulations 2018 and US Sec 482

groupRules.name: Internal price band
groupRules.rule: Goods or services sold between group businesses are priced at 80% to 100% of the market price shown; the engine blocks any price outside the band. Own-supply synergy bonuses apply on top.
groupRules.simplifiedFrom: Arm's-length principle in FIRS Transfer Pricing Regulations 2018 (simplified to a fixed band)

groupRules.name: Owner dividend
groupRules.rule: Parent pays the owner 20% of parent cash left after rule 1 each month, minus 10% withholding tax. Owner can raise the payout to 50% but each extra 10 points cuts the next month's upgrade budget by 10%.
groupRules.simplifiedFrom: Board-declared dividends with withholding tax at source (Nigeria); Berkshire's reinvest-first policy

groupRules.name: Control stake
groupRules.rule: The parent must hold at least 51% of every business. A share sale that would drop below 51% is blocked.
groupRules.simplifiedFrom: CBN 2026 draft holdco rules (51% in each subsidiary) and control tests in company law

groupRules.name: List a subsidiary
groupRules.rule: Allowed after 12 profitable game months in a row. Sell 10% to 49% of shares for (annual profit x 8) x share sold. Afterwards that share of the business's dividend goes to outside holders every month.
groupRules.simplifiedFrom: Exchange listing rules (track record of profits) and a typical 8x price-to-earnings on NGX

groupRules.name: Limited liability
groupRules.rule: If a business runs out of cash for 3 months, it closes; the parent loses only its stake and loans to it, unless it signed a guarantee. Total guarantees capped at 20% of group equity.
groupRules.simplifiedFrom: Limited liability of subsidiaries; CBN draft cap of contingent liabilities at 20% of shareholders' funds

groupRules.name: Capital hurdle
groupRules.rule: A new business or upgrade is shown green if expected yearly profit / cost >= 18%, amber 10-18%, red under 10%. Red builds are allowed but Zainab warns first.
groupRules.simplifiedFrom: Hurdle-rate capital budgeting used by holding companies (cost of equity in Nigeria roughly 18-20%, estimated)

bankInsideGroup.realRuleUS: Fed Reserve Act Sec 23A/Regulation W: a bank's loans to one affiliate <=10% of its capital, all affiliates <=20%, secured by 100-130% collateral; Sec 23B: market terms only. The Bank Holding Company Act largely bars bank owners from commercial businesses.
bankInsideGroup.realRuleNigeria: CBN: all insider-related credit (incl. group companies) <=10% of the bank's shareholders' funds, <=1% per director or big shareholder. Financial holdcos may not own non-financial firms, must hold 51% of each subsidiary.
bankInsideGroup.gameRule: Bank and Investment Bank sit in a ring-fenced Financial Arm. Bank loans to group firms: <=5% of bank equity each, <=10% in total, 120% collateral, same rate as outside customers. Bank cash cannot be dragged to other cards.

taxAndDividends: Each business pays 30% income tax plus a 4% development levy on profit (businesses under N50m turnover pay 0%), so tax is never pooled to dodge it. Dividends between group companies are not taxed again. Businesses keep 30% of after-tax profit and send 70% up. The parent pays the owner 20% of its free cash monthly, less 10% withholding; the owner's pocket buys the house, cars, travel and Legacy gifts, never business upgrades.

inflationControl: Costs scale with size: salaries rise 3% per staff level, and upkeep per business = 1% of its build cost a month. Tax takes 34% of profit. Synergy bonuses cap at +60% per business. Diminishing returns: each extra branch of a type earns 5% less (floor 50%). Big sinks: licences, Legacy gifts, the tower, heir training. Idle parent cash above 12 months of profit earns 0%.
openQuestions: Master storyline says internal loans at 5%: per month, per year, or flat? This file assumes 1% a month (12% a year).
The 9% farm loan synergy breaks the 'same terms as outside customers' bank rule. Make it a public farm scheme open to all farmers?
Should owner dividend stay 20% fixed, or let the player choose 10-50% with the upgrade-budget penalty in groupRules?
Should listed subsidiaries' outside shareholders vote, e.g. block a sale below 51% or demand a minimum dividend?
Is a game month always 7 real days for every business, or do slow businesses (Energy, Real Estate) need longer cycles?

sources.claim: Berkshire Hathaway reported $47.4bn operating earnings in 2024, paid $26.8bn to the IRS and has paid one cash dividend since 1965.
Danaher's FY2024 revenue was $23.9bn with net earnings of $3.9bn and free cash flow of $5.3bn.
Dangote Group had $5.4bn revenue in 2022, targeted about $30bn by 2025, and cement was about 75% of revenue.
Transcorp's FY2024 revenue was N407.9bn, 82.8% from power, with N94bn profit after tax and a N1.00 total dividend per share.
Section 23A limits a bank's covered transactions to 10% of capital for one affiliate and 20% for all affiliates.
Regulation W implements Sections 23A and 23B, including collateral and market-terms requirements for affiliate transactions.
CBN caps aggregate insider-related credit at 10% of shareholders' funds and 1% per director or significant shareholder, with subsidiaries counted as insiders.
CBN's 2026 draft financial holdco rules bar non-financial investments, require a 51% stake in each subsidiary and cap contingent liabilities at 20% of shareholders' funds.
The CBN proposed in June 2026 that holdcos keep at least 51% equity in each subsidiary.
Nigeria Tax Act 2025 sets 30% company income tax, 0% for small companies, and a 4% development levy, effective 1 January 2026.
The 2025 reform raises company capital gains tax to 30% and sets a 15% minimum effective tax rate for large groups.
Nigeria's 2018 Transfer Pricing Regulations require connected-party transactions to follow the arm's-length principle.
US after-tax ROIC by industry: software 54%, hospitals 29%, hotels 25%, education 27%, air transport 11.6%, power 7%, real estate development 7.2%.
The Bank Holding Company Act limits bank holding companies to banking and activities closely related to banking.
